about: The year each center started, for the growth-of-Chabad video (the owner's idea, Nov 6). Keyed by the center's chabad.org id (web/data/centers.geojson). 'year' is when the shluchim began there (their arrival or first activity); when the opening came later, the note says so. 'how': stated (the center or a paper says the year), list (a published list of institutions with years; therebbesimpact.com, unsourced, counts only as a lead, so 'low'), news (a report from that year), anniversary ("N years ago" counted back), directory (a dated directory listing or IRS record; as a last resort, when its chabad.org listing was made: the listing numbers run in order of creation, so a number dates the listing to within about a year, which bounds the start but is not it); first-mention (the year of the earliest mention found, used as the year); range ('after'/'by' bound it, no exact year); same-place (no year of its own, at the same spot as a dated one); not-found. 'confidence': high (a report from that year, or the center itself, and nothing against it), medium (counted back from 'N years ago', a first mention, one secondary source, or sources a year apart), low (one weak source, unconfirmed); range (no year: 'after'/'by' bound it from dated sources); open (no real source yet: 'year' is null and 'lead' holds a guess from therebbesimpact.com or the chabad.org listing number, only to check, never to use as a year. Owner, Nov 6: "basically a guess is ridiculous how can I use that in an expansion map"). A dot on the map takes the earliest year of its listings. Pilot: the Michigan shetach, Nov 6 (work/founding-years/michigan-pilot.md). 'date' (when one turns up, owner, Nov 6: "More data never hurt nobody"): the month or the day, 'YYYY-MM' or 'YYYY-MM-DD', of the same event as 'year'. 'shetach': the shetach id (data/shetachim.json); 'none' = Monsey, left blank on the map. 'earlier' (when found): the places a center used to be, oldest first, each {where, from, until, source} (years when known, else null); the map's dot is where it is now. Owner, Nov 6: "if you ever realize a center used to be located somewhere else then take note for the data". 'season' (owner, Nov 6: "or season which equates to a range ofc"): when only a season turns up for the same event as 'year' ('winter', 'spring', 'summer', 'fall'; or 'High Holidays', 'Chanukah' and the like).

Nine Mile Road' in Aug 1963 (Jewish News); its building there was dedicated in Dec 1958 under its earlier rabbi, so when it became Lubavitch between 1958 and 1963 is not pinned down. (Corrected: the first pass had 1958, from a 2003 article's '45-year-old Lubavitch congregation'.)

119459.name: Lubavitch Mikvah
119459.note: The men's mikvah at Mishkan Israel, 14000 W. Nine Mile (listed 2002): no year of its own; same place as Mishkan Israel (1958).

160382.name: Cheder Oholei Yosef Yitzchak Lubavitch - Boys Division
160382.note: The boys' division of the Lubavitch Cheder, founded 1965 (see Oholei Yosef Yitzchak Lubavitch). (A 1999 directory says 1958.)

118185.name: Yeshivas Lubavitch
118185.note: Detroit Jewish News, 4 July 2024, 'Since the Rebbe's Passing: over the past 30 years, these Chabad institutions have been founded in Michigan': 'Yeshivas Menachem Mendel Lubavitch/Mesivta - 1994' (taken to be this listing, Yeshivas Lubavitch, Oak Park). CrownHeights.info (Feb 2011) dates the high school to 1995; the school it grew from goes back to 1965. Also: a program 'started in Michigan out of the Yeshivas Menachem Mendel Lubavitch eight years ago' (Jewish News, Aug 2002) -> it existed in 1994.

119943.name: Ganeinu - Pre School
119943.note: April 1991: Bais Chabad of Farmington Hills launching a pre-nursery, 'Ganeinu Gan', for fall 1991 (Detroit Jewish News); a new facility at 4230 Middlebelt Rd, West Bloomfield, in 1992.

119944.name: Ganeinu Day Camp
119944.note: The Ganeinu day camp: no year of its own found; same place as the Ganeinu preschool (1991).

117639.name: Chabad House of Ann Arbor
117639.note: Founded by Chabad of Michigan in 1975 (Michigan Daily, 2005); a 1975 Detroit Jewish News notice names the director, Rabbi Aaron Y. Goldstein of Brooklyn.

117640.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Michigan
117640.note: In 1958 the Rebbe sent Rabbi Berel and Batsheva Shemtov to Detroit (Detroit Jewish News, 12 Sept 1958: 'Chabad Has Finally Arrived in Detroit'); the Lubavitch Foundation of Michigan was organized in 1959. Began in Detroit, now in Oak Park.

117643.name: Oholei Yosef Yitzchak Lubavitch
117643.note: Founded in 1965: at the 2011 groundbreaking of the Zekelman campus Rabbi Berel Shemtov read 'the original blessing from the late Lubavitcher Rebbe at the founding of the school in 1965' (Detroit Jewish News, 21 July 2011); CrownHeights.info, Feb 2011: 'Founded in 1965, the institution expanded in the 1980s to include a middle school; the high school was established in 1995.' (A 1999 directory says 1958.)

117641.name: Chabad House of Farmington Hills
117641.note: The Bergsteins have run the Bais Chabad of Farmington Hills since 1977 (Detroit Jewish News, 2023); Aug 1978: 'Chabad Congregation Open in Farmington, Rabbi Named'. Checked: the first archive mention is April 1978 ('Rabbi Chaim M. Bergstein, director of Cong. Bais Chabad of Farmington Hills'), so 1977 or 1978.

117642.name: Chabad House Lubavitch of Eastern Michigan
117642.note: Dec 2022: 'Thirty-seven years ago, Rabbi Yisroel Weingarten and his wife, Shainie, moved from Brooklyn to meet the needs of the Flint Jewish community' (Detroit Jewish News) -> 1985. Checked: not in Chabad's Michigan listings of 1980-81; 'Chabad House of Eastern Michigan' first appears in Dec 1986 - fits 1985. Checked (Nov 7): Michigan Jewish History, Fall 2012 (Jewish Historical Society of Michigan): 'Rabbi Yisroel Weingarten and his wife Shainie Chana established the Chabad House of Eastern Michigan in 1987', in its 25th year. The year kept is their arrival (1985, 'thirty-seven years ago' in Dec 2022); the Chabad House as such is 1987. Medium.

117644.name: F.R.E.E. Russian Jewry Center
117644.note: F.R.E.E. of Michigan (Chabad's organization for Soviet immigrants) began in 1990: its synagogue center under Rabbi Yosef Mishulovin opened 18 Aug 1990 (Jewish News ad, 17 Aug 1990) and F.R.E.E. is listed at 25615 Greenfield, Southfield, in Dec 1990. Its present Southfield building is later.

117645.name: Chabad Torah Center of West Bloomfield
117645.note: Rabbi Elimelech and his wife came to West Bloomfield in November 1975 as Lubavitch emissaries (the congregation's site); a minyan in rented space began in 1974 (CrownHeights.info, 'Silberbergs Honored for 40 Years of Shlichus').

117711.name: Chabad House-Lubavitch of Greater Toledo
117711.note: Rabbi Shemtov and his family brought Chabad House to Toledo in 1987, at first from their home on Secor Road (Toledo Blade, 2018). Checked: listed as Chabad House of Toledo, Rabbi Yosef Y. Shemtov, in May 1987 (Jewish News).

117989.name: Michigan Jewish Institute
117989.note: Founded in 1994, funded by the Lubavitch Foundation of Michigan. CLOSED 2 March 2016 after losing federal aid: the directory listing is out of date.

117993.name: Friendship Circle
117993.note: Detroit Jewish News, 4 July 2024, 'Since the Rebbe's Passing: over the past 30 years, these Chabad institutions have been founded in Michigan': 'Friendship Circle - 1994'. Also: 'the 8-year-old Friendship Circle' (Jewish News, Oct 2002).

118292.name: The Shul - Jack & Miriam Shenkman Building
118292.note: Nov 1994: Lubavitch of Michigan brought Rabbi Kasriel and Itty Shemtov to West Bloomfield; 'the Shul', the planned synagogue outreach center of the Campus of Living Judaism, not yet built (Jewish News); the July 2024 list also gives 1994.

118522.name: Chabad of Commerce
118522.note: Established in 2002 by Rabbi Schneor and Estie Greenberg (the center's site); began as Chabad Jewish Center of Commerce/Walled Lake in their townhouse (Jewish News).

118564.name: Beis Chabad of North Oak Park
118564.note: Detroit Jewish News, 9 Nov 1990: Friends of Refugees of Eastern Europe, an affiliate of Michigan Chabad, 'established Bais Chabad of North Oak Park at the Northgate Clubhouse in mid-August', for Soviet immigrants, led by Rabbi Yosef Mishulovin.

118632.name: Chabad House of Western Michigan
118632.note: Detroit Jewish News, 9 Sept 1977: 'Grand Rapids Site of Second Chabad House Student Unit' - Chabad-Lubavitch of Michigan announces the opening of a new Chabad House in Grand Rapids, director Rabbi Yosef Weingarten of Brooklyn. (Corrected: the first pass had 'about 1979', counted back from 'about nine years ago' in 1988.)

119457.name: Camp Gan Israel-Kalkaska
119457.note: Camp Gan Israel Detroit, 'Established 5721 - 1961' (shluchim.org camp directory); now in Kalkaska Township.

119721.name: Oholei Yosef Yitzchak Lubavitch - Mesivta
119721.note: The Detroit Lubavitch Yeshivah and Mesivta: 'Since 1965, the Lubavitch Yeshivah and Mesivta has been providing education for high school and junior college male students' (Detroit Jewish News, 14 July 2011); its middle school was added in the 1980s and the high school (Yeshivas Menachem Mendel) in 1994-95 (CrownHeights.info, Feb 2011; the July 2024 Jewish News list).

119974.name: Gan Yeladim Preschool
119974.note: Toledo Jewish News, June/July 2025: the preschool opened 35 years ago, with Raizel Shemtov from the start -> about 1990.

119975.name: Food & Learning Center
119975.note: Nothing found (Toledo Blade and Toledo Jewish News searched).

160380.name: The Wilmos & Lillian Schwarcz Education Center - Girls Building
160380.note: The Lubavitch Cheder's girls' building at 25401 Coolidge Hwy, Oak Park: the girls' elementary school is there in the Sept 1999 directory (a 1997 article has Lubavitch converting an old church into its girls' school); named for Lillian Schwarcz, who died in March 1999; enlarged 2007.

217615.name: Lubavitch Outreach
217615.note: First mention: 'Oak Park Chabad Lubavitch Outreach, Director: Rabbi Yosef Keselman' in the Jewish News, 25 May 2001; listed again in 2007 with Rabbi Yitzchok Mann among the shluchim. Founded by 2001.

393834.name: Chabad of Novi
393834.note: Jewish News, 12 Jan 2006: 'In the three months since Rabbi Avrohom and Leah Susskind began the Chabad Jewish Center of Novi-Northville...'; before moving from Oak Park they held a first program in Novi, Purim at the Novi Civic Center, March 2005. (Corrected: the July 2024 list says 2000.)

792116.name: The Friendship House
792116.note: The Daniel B. Sobel Friendship House: planned in 2001-2002; by Nov 2004 it had a director (Rabbi Yisrael Pinson) and its 2,500 sq ft building was due to open in spring 2005 (Jewish News). (Corrected: the July 2024 list's '1994' is Friendship Circle's year.)

953328.name: Chabad-Lubavitch of Bingham Farms
953328.note: Detroit Jewish News (4 July 2024) list of Michigan Chabad institutions founded since 1994: 'Chabad-Lubavitch of Bingham Farms - 2009'. Only this list gives 2009; the first Jewish News mention found is Dec 2016.

2435135.name: Chabad of Greater Downtown Detroit
2435135.note: Rabbi Yisrael Pinson named emissary for downtown Detroit in April 2013; the house at 278 Mack Ave opened with an open house on 16 Jan 2014 (Jewish News, Dec 2013 and Feb 2014).

3393324.name: Chabad Jewish Center of Bloomfield Hills
3393324.note: Chabad.org, 19 Oct 2016: 'co-directors of the recently founded Chabad of Bloomfield Hills', the Dubovs having just moved to the Detroit area; the Jewish News (2020) also says 2016. The July 2024 list's 2017 is a year off.

3829994.name: MSU Chabad
3829994.note: Detroit Jewish News (4 July 2024) list: 'Chabad Student Center at MSU - 2018'; founded by Rabbi Bentzion and Simi Shemtov (Jewish News, 2019).

4040602.name: Royal Oak Chabad Jewish Center
4040602.note: Nov 2018: the Royal Oak Jewish Center newly opened by Rabbi Moishie and Mushky Glitsenstein (myjewishdetroit.org); the July 2024 Jewish News list also gives 2018.

4428829.name: Chabad Jewish Center of Troy
4428829.note: March 2020: Chana Caytak moved back to Metro Detroit 'last year' and opened the Chabad Jewish Center of Troy with her husband, Rabbi Menachem Caytak (Jewish News); Nov 2021: 'more than two years after opening'.

5288480.name: Chabad of Livonia
5288480.note: Sept 2022: the Shemtovs moved to Livonia about six months earlier and launched the center (Jewish News); the July 2024 list also gives 2022.

5764141.name: Chabad Traverse City
5764141.note: Detroit Jewish News, 4 July 2024, 'Since the Rebbe's Passing: over the past 30 years, these Chabad institutions have been founded in Michigan': 'Chabad Jewish Community Center of Traverse City - 2023'. July 2024: 'a new center in Traverse City, where ... the emissary bought a building in the first year' (Jewish News).

6543662.name: Chabad Jewish Center of Waterford
6543662.note: Detroit Jewish News, 4 July 2024, 'Since the Rebbe's Passing: over the past 30 years, these Chabad institutions have been founded in Michigan': 'Chabad Jewish Center of Waterford - 2024'. Jewish News, 4 July 2024: Rabbi Berel Grossbaum 'arrived in Michigan earlier this month ... to launch the Waterford Chabad'.

1851659.name: Chabad Jewish Centre of Windsor
1851659.note: Congregation Shaarey Zedek, Windsor: 'Rabbi Galperin became the rabbi at Congregation Shaarey Zedek in June, 2009.' CrownHeights.info, 2 Aug 2012 (https://crownheights.info/shlichus/45935/canadian-towns-jewish-community-revitalized): local families 'three years ago welcomed Rabbi Sholom and Rivka Galperin into their community'; they 'established a Chabad House separate from the synagogue in their home' (no year given for that). Essex County, Ontario is in the Michigan shetach (owner, Oct 1); the first pass of the pilot left it out.

117632.name: Shaloh House Chabad of the South Area
117632.note: His profile: 'In the summer of 1987, Rabbi Gurkow started and led a community Shabbat Service at the Shaloh House in Stoughton, MA ... they moved to Stoughton, MA to start the Shaloh House Lubavitch Educational Center.' Stoughton Journal (COLlive, 'And then I met Chabad'): 'Gurkow first got involved in the mid '80s.' (GuideStar's 1991 is the IRS ruling year.)

117651.name: Chabad-Lubavitch of Nebraska
117651.note: The center's own building site: 'Touching Hearts since 1986'; a 2018 feature: the Katzmans were assigned to Omaha in 1986 (chaptzem.blogspot.com, 'Joyful Hasidic couple have spread light'). A 1992 notice spoke of 'five years of consistent programming' and a 2005 article of the 18th anniversary, both 1987: the first programs may be 1987.

117790.name: Chabad-Lubavitch of the Maritimes
117790.note: 24 Jan 2008: 'Thirteen years ago, Chabad representatives Rabbi Mendel and Bassie Feldman and one month old Zevi moved to Halifax to stay.' Anash.org: shluchim in Halifax 'since 5755 (1995), when they established Chabad Lubavitch of the Maritimes' (5755 = autumn 1994 to summer 1995).

118662.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Idaho
118662.note: Its About page: 'Rabbi & Mrs. Lifshitz moved to Boise in April 2004 to establish Chabad Lubavitch of Idaho'; the Idaho Statesman, 5 Dec 2004, on their arrival (jewishidaho.com/Article.asp?AID=239998). The first Chabad shluchim in Idaho.

3610901.name: Chabad of Newfoundland
3610901.note: The Chernitskys moved from Montreal to St. John's in February 2017 (CrownHeights.info, 'New Shluchim to Newfoundland'; Jewish Press, 1 Mar 2017, 'Chabad opens up store in Newfoundland', with their belongings being packed in Montreal).

117902.name: Lubavitch of Arkansas
117902.note: Congressional Record, 27 Mar 2025 (guest chaplain): Rabbi Ciment moved to Little Rock with his wife in 1992; his profile (opensiddur.org): 'In 1992, he and his wife established themselves in Little Rock, Arkansas as Shluchim'; the Jewish Virtual Library lists Lubavitch of Arkansas (1992). One UALR page says 'founded in 1993'.

300488.name: Chabad of Northwest Arkansas
300488.note: A dedication report: Chabad 'has been providing services to the local community and visitors since 2005'; Jewish Press (May 2015) on its decade of service. The Greismans first set up in Rogers, next to Bentonville.

672689.name: Chabad-Lubavitch of Wyoming
672689.note: 8 May 2008: 'Rabbi Zalman and Raizy Mendelsohn arrived in the mountainous state of Wyoming on Thursday' to open the state's first Chabad center (the Jackson Hole Star-Tribune gave May 6). In 2023 they had been Wyoming's only shluchim 'for the past 15 years'. (therebbesimpact.com's 2007 is wrong.)

5568314.name: Chabad of Laramie
5568314.note: The Raskins were sent to Laramie and Cheyenne on Yud Alef Nissan (2 Apr 2023), Wyoming's governor proclaiming the day; Laramie Live (Oct 2023): they 'moved to Laramie earlier this year' to open Wyoming's second Chabad center. (therebbesimpact.com's 2022 is wrong.)

117586.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Delaware
117586.note: 'Chabad of Delaware was launched in 1987, recalled Rabbi Chuni Vogel'; elsewhere 'established in 1987'; CrownHeights.info: the Vogels, 'regional directors of Chabad-Lubavitch of Delaware since 1987'.

117922.name: Chabad UD
117922.note: UDaily (Sept 2021): 'Rabbi Chuni Vogel, who founded Chabad in 1987 and is the father of its current leader, Rabbi Avremel Vogel'; Newark Post (2020): he started the Chabad Center 33 years ago in Park Place Apartments. Avremel and Shulie Vogel took it over in 2016-17.

5572560.name: Chabad of Southern Delaware
5572560.note: Spotlight Delaware (Apr 2025): Seaside Jewish Community was Sussex County's only synagogue 'until the establishment of Chabad of Southern Delaware in 2022'; Cape Gazette, Dec 2022: since its arrival 'some seven months ago' (spring 2022). Rabbi Sholom and Chanale Vogel.

117638.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Maine
117638.note: Its staff page: 'He arrived in Portland, Maine together with his wife Chana in 1987'; a Portland Press Herald piece by his son and a 2019 travel article ('since 1987') agree.

3104100.name: Chabad of Bangor
3104100.note: Congregation Beth Abraham's site: 'Rabbi Chaim Wilansky, his wife Esther, and their three children moved to Bangor in August of 2015'; the Maine Jewish clergy index has him there '2015 - present'. A 2019 travel article calls Chabad of Bangor 'established two years ago' (2017): the Chabad house as such may date from then. Checked (Nov 7): COLlive, Aug 24 2015 ('New Shluchim to Maine', https://collive.com/new-shluchim-to-maine/): 'Rabbi Chaim and Esther Wilansky (nee Polter) and their son Mendel will be moving on Shlichus this week to Bangor, Maine', 'establishing the first Chabad House in Northern Maine'. A report from the year itself, so high.

3858664.name: Chabad of Brunswick
3858664.note: Its fundraising page: 'since 2018, Chabad of Midcoast Maine has been servicing the educational, social and religious needs of the Jewish community in Brunswick'. Rabbi Shmuly and Draizy Lefkowitz; serves Bowdoin. Its own site gives no year.

117652.name: Chabad of New Hampshire
117652.note: 'Chabad Lubavitch of New Hampshire, founded in 1989'; the Krinskys 'have been based out of central Manchester since 1989'. The state's first Chabad house.

118602.name: Chabad at Dartmouth
118602.note: The Dartmouth, Sept 2003: 'Chabad Lubavitchers open Hanover center' (Moshe and Chani Gray, from Brooklyn, that fall); Dartmouth Alumni Magazine: 'founded in the fall of 2003 by Moshe and Chani Gray'.

3913111.name: Seacoast Chabad Jewish Community Center
3913111.note: 10 Feb 2018: Rabbi Berel and Rochy Slavaticki 'have been appointed as new shluchim' to the University of New Hampshire (Durham); NH Magazine: they moved from New York in 2018, outgrew two storefronts and bought the Newington campus. (therebbesimpact.com's 2017 is a year early.)

117712.name: Chabad House Lubavitch
117712.note: A Derher profile: 'Since 5747' (1987) Rabbi Yehuda and Etel Weg have served; they arrived in Oklahoma 'right after Pesach' (spring 1987). Chabad of Oklahoma's first house.

118273.name: Chabad Community Center For Jewish Life and Learning
118273.note: Lubavitch.com, 22 May 2019: 'When Rabbi Ovadia and Nechoma Goldman came to town in 1998, they were told Oklahoma City was reform country.' (Another Chabad report calls them founders in 1997.) First called Chabad of Oklahoma City.

5941552.name: Lubavitch Chabad of Norman
5941552.note: 27 Aug 2023: 'Rabbi Mendel and Basya Goldman who have been appointed as the new Shluchim to Norman, Oklahoma', the state's third.

117787.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Alberta
117787.note: The Jewish Historical Society of Southern Alberta's description of its archive: Chabad became a full-time presence in Calgary in 1988 with the arrival of Rabbi Menachem and Rochel Matusof; its emissaries first came in 1981 to run a summer day camp. Its own site and a CrownHeights.info profile give 1988; one Lubavitch.com piece says 1986.

117898.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Edmonton
117898.note: Alberta Jewish News, 6 Jan 2017: Chabad 'celebrated their twenty-fifth anniversary as part of the Jewish Community of Edmonton' (Dec 2016), 'the twenty-five years since Rabbi Ari arrived'; a community directory: 'since its founding in 1991 ... led by Rabbi Ari Drelich'. (The Alberta archive says an Edmonton branch opened in 1990; another listing says 1992.)

6076916.name: Chabad of the Canadian Rockies
6076916.note: Chabad.org (late 2023), 'Banff and Canadian Rockies Gets Its First Full Time Rabbi': the Pinsons moved to the Banff region 'this past fall' to open it; Chabad of Alberta's own materials: the Canmore branch opened in 2023 (CrownHeights.info, Sept 2023, 'Veteran Shluchim Pioneering a New Frontier').

117895.name: Chabad Lubavitch Jewish Center of Merrimack Valley
117895.note: Wicked Local, 1 Oct 2013: Rabbi Asher Bronstein, 'Just like when we came 21 years ago (to Andover)'. Not settled: the Lawrence History Center holds the 'Chabad Lubavitch of the Merrimack Valley First Annual Founders' Dinner' journal, dated only 'c. 1990'; Merrimack Valley Lubavitch Inc.'s IRS ruling is 1994. Checked (Nov 7): its own staff page (https://www.chabadmv.com/templates/articlecco_cdo/aid/2194385/jewish/Our-Rabbis-Rebbetzins.htm): 'Rabbi Asher Bronstein, together with his wife Faigy ... has been serving the local Jews in the Merrimack Valley since 1992'. Two sources agree, so high (the 'c. 1990' founders' dinner journal is undated).

118492.name: Chabad of Nashoba Valley
118492.note: CrownHeights.info, 2 Oct 2005: 'The newly established Chabad Center for Nashoba Valley, at 26 Tadmuck Road', Rabbi Zalman and Malkie Gurkow; moved in that July, open house 18 Sept. It follows 'the Chabad-based Nashoba Valley Jewish Center, which operated in Westford under Rabbi Mayshe Schwartz' (IRS ruling May 2001), so Chabad in Westford is older.

3792602.name: Anshe Sholom Chabad of Greater Haverhill
3792602.note: Eagle-Tribune, 19 Sept 2017, 'Jewish groups merge to form new congregation': Anshe Sholom and Rabbi Zalman Borenstein's Chabad (of North Andover, opened by 2013) became Anshe Sholom Chabad at the new year. (Read through Firecrawl; the paper refused a plain fetch.)

117910.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Utah
117910.note: The Zippels came to Salt Lake City in 1992 (the Rebbe's blessing 1 Mar 1992); most reports say July 1992 (others fall, or April); 25 years marked in 2018, 30 in 2022 (KSL).

1962343.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Park City
1962343.note: Chabad Lubavitch of Utah's own page ('Chabad Lubavitch of Utah has opened a center in Park City'): 'In September 2012 Chabad Lubavitch of Utah added a full-time Chabad presence in Park City. Rabbi Yudi and Mrs. Devori Steiger serve as directors of Chabad of Park City'. Earlier entry: Chabad.org (via COLlive): 'Since 2013, Rabbi Yudi and Devori Steiger have directed the Park City Chabad-Lubavitch Community Center.' One source; a summary of other coverage said Chabad came to Park City in 2012, but no source for that was found. Checked (Nov 7): the Utah page gives Sept 2012 and Chabad.org 'since 2013', a year apart, so medium; the year taken is the specific one.

4100713.name: Chabad Jewish Community Center of Southern Utah
4100713.note: Lubavitch.com, 18 Oct 2018: 'Rabbi Mendy and Chaya Cohen, and their two young children, are setting up shop in St. George.'

5643848.name: Chabad of Utah County
5643848.note: Rabbi Chaim and Esty Zippel moved to Utah County and set up Chabad of Utah County in Lehi in the first week of December 2022 (KSL); the county commission's proclamation, 29 Mar 2023.

117927.name: Lubavitch Jewish Center of Alaska
117927.note: Jewish Press: 'when Rabbi Yosef and Esther Greenberg arrived in Alaska in 1991 they set up the Chabad-Lubavitch Jewish Center of Alaska'; J. Weekly: they arrived in Anchorage in 1991 as newlyweds to set up Alaska's first Chabad center; a 1999 Detroit Jewish News item: established in 1991. (One profile says 1990.)

119784.name: The Alaskan Mikvah
119784.note: Mikvah.org's directory (Taharat Hamishpachah International): 'Tamar Tziporra Alaskan Mikvah ... Established 2002', 1701 East 36th Avenue, Anchorage, Lubavitch Jewish Center of Alaska, Rabbi Yosef Greenberg. It fits the earlier find that in June 2001 building a mikvah was the Greenbergs' first priority. A directory's year, so medium. Found by Firecrawl's research agent; the quote checked on the page.

3116169.name: Mat-Su Jewish Center Chabad Lubavitch
3116169.note: CrownHeights.info, 9 Nov 2015: Rabbi Mendy and Chaya Greenberg 'moved into their new home on a quiet dirt road in Wasilla, Alaska, one week before the High Holidays' (Sept 2015); a 2017 release: 'founded in 2015'.

6394348.name: Fairbanks Jewish Center - Chabad Lubavitch
6394348.note: Chabad.org (Dec 2024): Rabbi Heshy Wolf 'moved with his wife, Chani, in September of this year to establish the Chabad-Lubavitch Fairbanks Jewish Center'; Jewish Journal, Feb 2026: 'before the Wolfs' arrival 18 months ago'.

117950.name: Chabad of Columbus
117950.note: Rabbi Areyah Kaltmann: 'We began our work in New Albany in 1998.' The Kaltmanns themselves 'set out in 1991 to light up central Ohio', first as directors of the OSU Chabad House (its own page); that start is on the OSU dot.

349392.name: Schottenstein Chabad House
349392.note: Chabad Columbus: the Kaltmanns 'set out in 1991' and 'began their work in Central Ohio as Directors at the OSU Chabad House'. The Deitsch family has served OSU's students 'since 1996' (Columbus Jewish News); a ChabadInfo piece calls the house 'instituted 26 years ago'. So Chabad at OSU from 1991, its own house perhaps from 1996.

3660798.name: Chabad of Downtown Columbus
3660798.note: Its own About page: 'Rabbi Yitzi and Sara have been co-directing Chabad of Downtown Columbus since the summer of 2017.' (therebbesimpact.com and the listing number also point to 2017.)

6925466.name: Chabad of Bexley
6925466.note: No source found. therebbesimpact.com: Shea & Sarah Kaltmann, 2025; chabad.org's listing number (6925466) is a 2025 one.

118178.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Cape Cod
118178.note: Rabbi Yekusiel (Kuti) and Devorah Alperowitz have served Cape Cod and the islands 'since 1995' (a feature); Anash: 'for the past twenty-eight years'; the Cape News (Sept 2024): founded in Hyannis 'almost 30 years ago'.

5302137.name: Chabad on the Vineyard
5302137.note: Vineyard Gazette, Oct 2023: 'Rabbi Tzvi Alperowitz, who founded the Vineyard Haven Chabad house in 2021'; Chabad.org and JNS: they arrived in June to set up the island's first Chabad center; the Jewish Star: they docked in Vineyard Haven on June 8.

6286364.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Falmouth
6286364.note: Cape News, 20 Sept 2024: Rabbi Mendel Alperowitz 'recently moved to downtown Falmouth with Rochel and their three children'; services to begin the next month (Oct 2024), first a Rosh Hashana celebration. CrownHeights.info, 5 Mar 2025: they 'have established a new Chabad center in Falmouth'.

6525447.name: Chabad of Nantucket
6525447.note: No source found (Rabbi Levi Alperowitz). Estimated from chabad.org's listing number, 6525447, created about Nov 2024 (Fairbanks's, Sept 2024, is 6394348). A visitor guide names him; no date.

117691.name: Chabad of Rockland
117691.note: Its About page: 'Established in 1983 under the dedicated direction of Rabbi Avremel Kotlarsky and his wife, Chany.' A 2004 Chabad.org article: Rabbi Mordechai Altein bought the property in 1982 so the Achei Temimim school could move from the Bronx to New City; the building went up in 1991.

118346.name: Chabad of The Nyacks
118346.note: A listing for Rabbi Chaim Zvi and Chaya Ehrenreich's center: 'established in 2001 to serve the Jewish communities of southern Rockland County', then in Chestnut Ridge (a 2007 Journal News piece calls him 'Rabbi Chaim Ehrenreich from Chabad of Chestnut Ridge'). When it became Chabad of the Nyacks, in Nyack, not found. Checked (Nov 7): The Journal News (lohud), May 18 2010, reproduced on its site (https://www.chabadnyack.org/templates/articlecco_cdo/aid/1215597/jewish/New-Torah.htm): 'The Chabad Center, at 6 Whitefield Road in Chestnut Ridge ... was opened in 2001, Ehrenreich said.' So high.

577207.name: Chabad Jewish Center of Suffern
577207.note: No source found (its own site gives no year). therebbesimpact.com: 2007; chabad.org's listing number (577207) is from about 2007 too; the IRS ruling for Congregation Chabad Jewish Center of Suffern Inc. is March 2010. Directed by Rabbi Shmuel and Devorah Gancz (the directory still names Rabbi Isaac Lefkowitz).

5161431.name: Chabad Israel Center
5161431.note: No source found. therebbesimpact.com: Shneur Zalmen & Hodaya Haddad, 2021; chabad.org's listing number (5161431) is from about 2021. Running by Feb 2023 (CrownHeights.info).

6169151.name: Chabad of Stony Point
6169151.note: No source found. therebbesimpact.com: 'Chabad of Stony Point', 2023; chabad.org's listing number (6169151) is from about 2023. Rabbi Shea Werner (with Rabbi Shmuel Amram, per a congressional proclamation, COLlive); 17 Phillips Drive.

117966.name: American Friends of Lubavitch (Chabad)
117966.note: JTA (Dec 2020): Rabbi Levi Shemtov has run Chabad's Washington operations since 1992; Washington Jewish Week: in the early 1990s it worked out of a small Capitol Hill townhouse; the $2 million center in the embassy district opened in July 1999 (Washington Post). American Friends of Lubavitch itself, under Rabbi Abraham Shemtov, was active in Washington by 1984.

749420.name: Chabad GW
749420.note: Jewish Washington's directory: Chabad GW 'founded in 1994'; a listing: 'nearly 30 years'. Its first full-time campus couple, the Steiners, came only in 2008 (the Washingtonian, 2015); in 1994 it was American Friends of Lubavitch's program. Checked (Nov 7): its own site (https://www.chabadgw.com/about): 'Ever since this program began in the early 90's' — not more exact, so it stays medium.

1944096.name: Chabad Lubavitch of the AU Community
1944096.note: CrownHeights.info, 23 Aug 2012: 'Rabbi Yehoshua and Esti Hecht will iy"h be moving to the American University Area in Northwest Washington, DC', appointed by Rabbi Levi Shemtov.

3077645.name: Chabad Georgetown
3077645.note: COLlive, 30 Aug 2021: 'Chabad Georgetown formally commenced operations this week in a new premises two blocks from the main campus', Rabbi Menachem and Racheli Shemtov; before that a satellite program of American Friends of Lubavitch 'for years', and the couple worked from a basement first (its brochure: in early 2020 they 'wanted to come to Georgetown').

5154542.name: Chabad East DC Jewish Center
5154542.note: COLlive, Aug 2021: Chabad East DC, Rabbi Yitzi and Shana Ceitlin, set up its Georgetown Law program 'during Covid-19' and was then launching a Capitol Hill minyan; therebbesimpact.com and chabad.org's listing number (5154542) both point to 2021. It may have begun in 2020.

117538.name: Chabad of Alabama
117538.note: A Chabad.org article: Rabbi Yosef Posner 'settled here with wife Frumie in 1987' (the Friedmans joined in 1993). But in the Huntsville Times (Sept 2010) Rabbi Posner recalled 'my beginning here in Birmingham (in the early '80s)' — perhaps visits before he settled. Checked (Nov 7): Southern Jewish Life, July 10 2026 ('Chabad of Alabama establishes a foundation', https://southernjewishlife.substack.com/p/chabad-of-alabama-establishes-a-foundation): 'Chabad in Birmingham was established in 1982, the Posners arrived in 1987.' That fits Rabbi Posner's 'my beginning here in Birmingham (in the early '80s)'; so the year is Chabad's start in Birmingham, 1982 (was 1987, the Posners' settling). Medium: who began it in 1982 isn't said.

7055697.name: Chabad on Wheels
7055697.note: CrownHeights.info, 18 June 2025: Rabbi Sholom Posner's Chabad on Wheels, crossing Alabama several times a year; no start date given. chabad.org's listing number (7055697) is from 2025. A mobile program of Chabad of Alabama.

1015137.name: Chabad of Huntsville
1015137.note: Huntsville Times (CrownHeights.info, 12 Sept 2010): 'Rabbi Laibel Berkowitz with his wife, Chanie, and 6-month-old daughter, Muka, have moved to the Huntsville area to establish the Chabad Jewish Center of North Alabama' (the listing number, 1015137, is from about then). Rabbi Moshe and Mushky Cohen founded today's Chabad of Huntsville in 2015 (SJL, 2023).

2541793.name: Chabad of Mobile
2541793.note: Chabad.org (2016, at the opening of the Olender Chabad House): 'it was only two years ago' that Mobile was added to Chabad's map; Anash (2025): 'in just 11 years' the Goldwassers; therebbesimpact.com: 2014. They came from Crown Heights after a first visit at Chanukah (SJL, 'Mobile gaining new Chabad presence').

2948851.name: Chabad at the University of Alabama
2948851.note: Chabad.org: 'Rabbi Kussi and Rosie Lipskier have been serving at the University of Alabama since 2015'; The Odyssey: 'in 2015 ... moved to Tuscaloosa to open the Chabad Jewish Center' (one of 19 campus centers opening that fall).

7392590.name: Chabad of Auburn
7392590.note: Anash, 8 July 2026: Rabbi Aryeh and Chana Wells 'will move to Auburn this fall' for Auburn University, building on Rabbi Shalom Posner's Chabad on Wheels. (Read through Firecrawl.)

117703.name: Chabad Jewish Center
117703.note: Its own '36 Year Gala' page (gala 16 Feb 2027): 'Thirty six years ago, Rabbi Yisroel and Chana Mangel arrived in Cincinnati' (1990 or 1991). GuideStar's ruling year for Congregation Lubavitch aka Chabad Jewish Center of Blue Ash is 1990. It began as Shabbat meals in the Mangels' Hunters Creek apartment, then a building on Kenwood Road; the Hunt Road center was in use from Sept 2004, grand opening 11 Sept 2005 (Community Press, 7 Sept 2005). Checked (Nov 7): Chabad.org News (Oct 2025, 'Chabad Rebbetzin named Cincinnati Enquirer Woman of the Year', https://www.chabad.org/news/article_cdo/aid/7093699): the Rebbe 'sent the Mangels to Cincinnati in 1990, where they established Chabad of Blue Ash'. So 1990, high.

117967.name: Chabad of Greater Dayton
117967.note: Dayton Jewish Observer (Apr 2023, its 30th anniversary gala): Rabbi Nochum Mangel, 'who with his wife, Devorah, was sent to Dayton in 1993 to establish a Chabad here'; they arrived 'in the summer of 1993'.

118177.name: The Jewish Discovery Center
118177.note: Its About page: Rabbi Yosef Kalmanson 'co-founded the Jewish Discovery Center in 1994 alongside his wife, Rochel'. GuideStar's ruling year for the Jewish Discovery Center of Ohio is 1998.

2124148.name: Chabad at the University of Cincinnati
2124148.note: Cincinnati Jewish Journal: Rabbi Yitzi Creeger 'began the programming for the UC Jewish community in 2006 with his wife, Dina Creeger'.

2342907.name: Chabad at Miami University
2342907.note: Oxford Observer: the Greenbergs came to look, 'and in November 2013 they moved in'. Dayton Jewish Observer, Jan 2014: 'Chabad comes to Miami U'.

6958605.name: Chabad Young Professionals Cincinnati
6958605.note: COLlive, 15 Sept 2025: Rabbi Levik and Mushky Gourarie 'will be moving to Eastside Cincinnati to launch the Eastside's first Chabad center'; Chabad.org (12 Oct 2025): a late-August meet-and-greet at Washington Park drew 40 young professionals.

117789.name: Chabad-Lubavitch of Winnipeg
117789.note: Its own Historical Outline of Growth: '1972: Lubavitch Centre established in Winnipeg by Rabbi A. Altein.' The CJN (13 July 2026): Rabbi Avrohom and Brocha Altein 'moved to Winnipeg in 1972'. (The same outline: South End branch on Grant Avenue 1994; Jewish Learning Centre on Mathers Avenue built from 2010, opened Chanukah 2011.)

3195061.name: Chabad Lubavitch Mikvah - NE Branch
3195061.note: The North End mikvah, 455 Hartford Avenue. Chabad Winnipeg's own outline, under 1978: 'Chabad Mikvah' built on Hartford Avenue. A CJN piece on the new south Winnipeg mikvah (2011-12) says Rabbi Altein built it 'more than 35 years ago'.

746050.name: The Friendship Circle
746050.note: No source found; its chabad.org listing gives no address or year. The listing number (746050) is from about 2008, so it existed by then. Rabbi Boruch and Chana Heidingsfeld are among Winnipeg's shluchim (therebbesimpact.com has them from 2000).

1344050.name: Chabad-Lubavitch of Saskatoon
1344050.note: COLlive, 25 July 2011: Rabbi Raphael and Sarah Kats 'moved from Brooklyn, N.Y., to Saskatoon one month ago' to open Saskatchewan's first Chabad house (the Saskatchewan Jewish Discovery Centre), in their home. The CJN also gives June 2011. He had visited as a rabbinical student in 2010.

2051293.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Regina
2051293.note: CrownHeights.info, 18 Apr 2013: the new Chabad center will 'open this summer in Regina'; Rabbi Avrohom and Shterna Simmonds 'will arrive in early summer' and had already run holiday programs there. Rabbi Altein: 'we never had a permanent presence there.'

4749846.name: Chabad Israeli Centre
4749846.note: Lubavitch.com, 17 Aug 2020: Rabbi Mendel and Dvora Altein 'will move to Winnipeg' to expand Chabad's work among the city's Hebrew speakers, with Hebrew programs and an after-school program. chabad.org's listing number (4749846) is from 2020 too.

117908.name: Chabad Lubavitch of the North Shore
117908.note: Lubavitch.com, 3 July 2005: Chabad of the North Shore 'began in 1992 with a small office in the oceanside town of Swampscott'; Rabbi Yossi and Layah Lipsker 'founded the organization in 1992' (also Lubavitch.com, 28 Oct 2024). Its IRS record dates from June 1993.

118611.name: Chabad of Peabody Jewish Center
118611.note: Chabad.org, 29 Apr 2021: as Covid began (spring 2020) Rabbi Nechemia and Raizel Schusterman 'were starting to plan for their 18th year of service to the Jewish community of Peabody' (so from 2003). Lubavitch.com, July 2005, calls Chabad of Peabody 'newly opened'. Its own building dedicated June 2015.

402434.name: Chabad of Beverly-Salem
402434.note: Lubavitch.com, 28 Oct 2024: Rabbi Mendel and Fraidy Barber 'moved to the North Shore in August 2023 to establish Chabad of Beverly-Salem', the fifth Chabad house on the North Shore.

3817417.name: Tobin Bridge Chabad
3817417.note: Boston Globe, 20 Sept 2017: 'the newly opened Tobin Bridge Chabad', at Congregation Tifereth Israel of Everett; Rabbi Sruli and Chaya Baron moved to Chelsea 'earlier this month' and were preparing their first Rosh Hashana there. Chabad had approached the Everett congregation about two years before.

5273687.name: Chabad of Cape Ann
5273687.note: Jewish Journal (North Shore, MA), Nov 18 2021 ('Chabad Lubavitch expands to Cape Ann in time to light the menorah'): 'Rabbi Avremi Raichik and his wife, Rivky, are settling into their new home in Gloucester ... while they go about opening a satellite of Chabad Lubavitch of the North Shore on Cape Ann just in time for Hanukkah.' (therebbesimpact.com: the center 2021.)

6192413.name: Chabad of Wakefield
6192413.note: COLlive, 21 Feb 2024: Rabbi Sruly and Devora Leah Brook are 'establishing a permanent Chabad presence in Wakefield, MA. and its surrounding towns' (an affiliate of Chabad of the North Shore); the Reading Post: opening ahead of Purim.

117962.name: Chabad of New Mexico
117962.note: Its About page: 'Established with the blessing of the Lubavitcher Rebbe in 1992', directed by Rabbi Chaim and Devorah Leah Schmukler. Open at 4000 San Pedro Blvd. NE by Dec 1995 (a bar mitzvah invitation in the Southwest Jewish Archives).

118225.name: Santa Fe Jewish Center-Chabad
118225.note: Lubavitch.com, 3 Sept 2002: Rabbi Berel and Devorah Leah Levertov 'arrived here in 1996'; they began in their home on Don Gaspar Avenue (a 1997 New Mexican article), then 15 years at San Mateo Road and Galisteo Street (from 2000), then 230 W. Manhattan Ave. (bought 2015, finished 2023). The New Mexican (Aug 2021) says 'arrived 24 years ago' (a year later) under the headline '25 years in the works'.

705397.name: Chabad of Taos
705397.note: The Canadian Jewish News, Jan 17 2020 (Sandy Bornstein, 'The remote Jews of Taos, N.M.'): 'Chabad has had a presence in Taos since 2008.' (Rabbi Eliyahu and Batsheva Kaminetzky; therebbesimpact.com and the listing number also point to 2008.) Found by Firecrawl's research agent; the quote checked on the page.

810309.name: Alevy Chabad Jewish Center de Las Cruces
810309.note: CrownHeights.info, 25 Apr 2022: 'in 2009, when the long-time residents of Las Cruces, New Mexico, heard that Chabad was coming to town'; Rabbi Bery Schmukler and his wife began in their dining room (first event a Sukkot party).

1601116.name: Mikvah Moshe
1601116.note: JTA, 11 Nov 2010: the Levertovs are 'about to complete construction on a mikvah' ('The building is, of course, adobe'). The Mosie and Chella Safra Mikvah, 1505 Galisteo St. (Mikvah.org). chabad.org's listing number (1601116) is from about 2011, so it opened late 2010 or in 2011. Checked (Nov 7): Chabad.org News, June 2 2010 ('Jewish Ritual Bath Makes History in New Mexico's City Different', https://www.chabad.org/news/article_cdo/aid/1222317): 'the grand opening of the Chella and Moise Safra Mikvah in Santa Fe ... the May 15 unveiling presided over by ... Rabbi Berel and DevorahLeah Levertov'. So 2010-05-15, high.

7309271.name: Chabad of Eldorado
7309271.note: COLlive, May 11 2026 ('New Shluchim To Eldorado, New Mexico'): 'This summer, Rabbi Levi and Sara Shemtov (née Levertov), will establish a Chabad House in Eldorado'. A report from the year itself. Found by Firecrawl's research agent; the quote checked on the page.

486805.name: Chabad-Lubavitch of Montana
486805.note: CrownHeights.info, 13 Mar 2007 (from the Bozeman press): 'A Jewish rabbi is moving here'; Chaim and Chavie Bruk 'intend to set up a base in Bozeman'. J. (Aug 2009): the Bruks 'arrived in Bozeman in early 2007'. Lubavitch.com (Feb 2022) says 'since arriving in Bozeman in 2006' (his first visit). The first permanent Chabad center in Montana.

888933.name: Mikvah Mei Menachem
888933.note: JTA, 7 May 2009: Montana's first mikveh has opened, in an extension of the Bruks' Bozeman home; it 'took two years to build'.

2502139.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Missoula
2502139.note: CrownHeights.info / Chabad.org (May 2023): after seven years of crossing the state, 'in 2014 the Bruks opened a second Chabad Lubavitch Center in Missoula', now led by Rabbi Chezky and Rochi Vogel (therebbesimpact.com has the Vogels from 2018).

3995931.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Flathead Valley
3995931.note: Queens Jewish Link interview: Rabbi Shneur and Chana Wolf 'moved to Kalispell in November of 2018, during a blizzard'; Montana's third Chabad center. A Chabad page: they 'opened this Chabad Center in 2018'.

5384373.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Billings
5384373.note: CrownHeights.info / Chabad.org (May 2023): the Billings center 'was founded just prior to the High Holidays of 2022 by Rabbi Shaul and Mushky Shkedi'. Announced on Lubavitch.com, 10 Feb 2022.

7117900.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Great Falls
7117900.note: No founding report found. Rabbi Mendel and Devorah Spiero were inviting Great Falls to Purim in March 2024 (Congregation Aitz Chaim's newsletter, 10 Mar 2024), so it ran by then; therebbesimpact.com has the couple from 2023. chabad.org's listing number (7117900) is from late 2025.

117621.name: Chabad of Kentucky
117621.note: Jewish Louisville, 'Chabad at 30' (22 Jan 2015): 'In March of 1985, Rabbi Avrohom and Goldie Litvin moved to Louisville' to open Chabad's branch for Kentucky; their first program was a Purim talk on the day they arrived. Its site: 'since 1985'. Its Chabad House on Almara Circle burned down in April 2022.

119753.name: Gan Torah
119753.note: The Louisville Jewish Day School 'first opened its doors as Gan Torah of Louisville – the Beverly Weisberg Preschool, in 1996' (a Chabad profile); WDRB (Mar 2014): 'The school opened in 1996'. The preschool and day school moved into the Jewish Learning Center on 6 Sept 2016.

347769.name: Louisville Jewish Day School
347769.note: WDRB (via CrownHeights.info, 26 Mar 2014), on Kentucky's only Jewish day school: 'The school opened in 1996 — but moved this year to the Starks Building.' It began as Gan Torah's preschool and kindergarten, became Torah Academy, and took the Louisville Jewish Day School name after Eliahu Academy closed (2006-08). Private School Review: founded 1996, and lists it as closed in 2025 (unconfirmed). Checked (Nov 7): the Chabad Chinuch Office's directory (2023-24) gives 'Founded: 1997', a year later, so it stays medium.

3483282.name: Jewish Learning Center
3483282.note: Jewish Louisville, 23 Nov 2016: the Jewish Learning Center at 1110 Dupont Circle 'is now open'; the day school and Gan Torah moved in on 6 Sept, ribbon-cutting 25 Sept (2016); Rabbi Shmully Litvin its community coordinator.

119428.name: Camp Gan Israel
119428.note: No start year found. Its camp page advertises the summer of 2011 (27 June - 22 July); its listing number (119428) is from chabad.org's first directory, so it likely ran well before. Run by Chabad of Kentucky (since 1985).

1763771.name: Chabad of Prospect
1763771.note: Its own About page (May 2018): 'In 2008, we moved to Lousiville and opened the Chabad Chai Center working with Chabad of Kentucky. After many successful years there, the need for an additional center in Prospect became readily apparent. The Chabad Chai Center moved to Prospect and opened on Lag Ba'Omer 2018' (Rabbi Boruch Susman; now 6900 Transylvania Ave, Prospect). Jewish Louisville (Apr 2012): Chabad of Kentucky 'will be opening a new center on March 25, 2012', the Chabad Chai Center at 8701 Shelbyville Road — a new home, not the start (the year was 2012 before this check). therebbesimpact.com: the Susmans from 2008.

earlier.where: its first premises in Louisville (2008)
8701 Shelbyville Road, Louisville (the new center opened March 25, 2012)

2922724.name: Chabad of the Bluegrass
2922724.note: Lexington's Jewish newsletter (Feb 2016) reports a 30 Nov 2015 meeting with Rabbi Shlomo and Shoshi Litvin about the 'new' Chabad House in Lexington; therebbesimpact.com: 2015. But CrownHeights.info (10 Nov 2016) says 'In their first year of operation' they outgrew the original house, which fits a start in 2016; so 2015 or 2016. Checked (Nov 7): Rabbi Litvin's own account (Dollar Daily, https://dollardaily.org/illuminations/156/pdf): 'Just before Purim of 2015, we moved to Lexington and began our shlichus.' So 2015 (March), high.

117608.name: Chabad of Hawaii
117608.note: Chabad.org, 18 Nov 2007: Rabbi Itchel and Pearl Krasnjansky 'arrived in August 1987 with a toddler'; 'the culmination of 20 years of Chabad-Lubavitch activities in Hawaii'. The Star-Bulletin (2001): they moved from New York about 14 years before.

1619165.name: Mikvas Batsheva
1619165.note: Chabad.org, 12 Nov 2010: 'First Kosher Ritual Bath Constructed in Honolulu'; its celebration that Sunday 'at the site of Mikvas Batsheva', named for Pearl Krasnjansky's mother, Batsheva Rotenstreich.

594376.name: Chabad Kauai
594376.note: No founding report found. chabad.org's listing number (594376) is from about Nov 2007 (an article of 18 Nov 2007 is 596066); a kosher directory says 'Since 2010'. Rabbi Michoel Goldman led Chabad of Kaua'i by Oct 2010 (its first Torah scroll, CrownHeights.info). He commuted from New York 'for many years' before the family moved to Kauai full-time (ChabadInfo), about 2021 by Chabad.org's 'past five years' (2026).

1051208.name: Chabad of Kona & West Hawaii
1051208.note: Its own page (Chabad of the Big Island, jewishbigisland): 'Launched in the Fall of 2009, Chabad has become the address for everything Jewish on the Big Island of Hawaii' (Rabbi Levi and Fraidy Gerlitzky; the same email, jewishbigisland@gmail.com, is on Chabad of Hawaii's list of centers). therebbesimpact.com (2009) and the listing number (about 2009) agree.

1329273.name: Chabad of Maui
1329273.note: Detroit Jewish News, 16 Mar 2006: 'a young Lubavitch couple, Sholom and Danit Shusterman, previously of Brooklyn, have set up shop as the Maui Mitzvah Center. They decided to move to Maui just after their February 2004 wedding.' Maui Time (28 Sept 2004) already reports the Maui Mitzvah Center. A directory names it 'Chabad of Maui Mitzvah Center'. therebbesimpact.com: Chabad of Maui 2005; Mendy and Mushka Krasnjansky from 2017. chabad.org's listing (1329273) is from about 2010. Checked (Nov 7): Maui Time already reported the Maui Mitzvah Center on 28 Sept 2004, a report from the year itself; the Jerusalem Post (Oct 11 2005, 'Mitzvot in Maui') carries the same account as the Detroit Jewish News ('just months after their February 2004 wedding'). So high.

5784680.name: Chabad of Hilo and East Side of the Big Island
5784680.note: Its launch campaign on Charidy ('Help Us Launch', Rabbi Yeshaya Rotenberg; it ended July 26 2023): 'Take part in the foundation of Chabad of Hilo! ... Chabad will serve as a center for Jewish life and education for the East of the Big Island of Hawaii'. Medium: the chabad.org listing (5784680) may date from late 2022, a few months before the launch.

6969026.name: CYP Oahu
6969026.note: No source found; no director listed. chabad.org's listing number (6969026) is from 2025 (CYP Cincinnati's, Sept 2025, is 6958605). A young professionals program of Chabad of Hawaii.

117619.name: Lubavitch of Indiana - Chabad Center for Jewish Life
117619.note: Chabad.org (16 Mar 2015, via CrownHeights.info): 'After 34 Years, New Home for Indiana Jewish Community' (Rabbi Avrohom and Nini Grossbaum, 'more than three decades in Indianapolis'). Their son's page: sent by the Rebbe 'in the early 1980's'. therebbesimpact.com: the couple from 1981. Checked (Nov 7): COLlive, June 6 2023 ('Mike Pence Joins Chabad Indiana Gala', https://collive.com/mike-pence-joins-chabad-indiana-gala-before-announcing-run/): 'Chabad of Indiana, led by Shluchim Rabbi Avrohom and Nini Grossbaum and Rabbi Dovid and Chana Grossbaum has been operating in Indiana since 1981', so high.

117944.name: Chabad House of Bloomington
117944.note: Lubavitch.com (13 Nov 2019): the new building 'far surpasses Chabad's home of 30 years' (so from about 1989), found by Rabbi Avrohom Grossbaum 'more than three decades ago'; 'In the early 1990s' the Grossbaums brought in Rabbi Yehoshua and Zlata Chincholker, 'Chabad's representatives here for 29 years' (about 1990). The Indiana Daily Student (2010): they 'opened the Chabad House in the 1980s'. therebbesimpact.com: the center 1993, the couple 1991. Checked (Nov 7): Anash.org (Aug 3 2020, new shluchim to Indiana University): the Chincholkers 'have been serving the vibrant Jewish student body for the past 29 years' (about 1991, their arrival); the Chabad House itself is from about 1989, so it stays medium.

117984.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Northwest Indiana
117984.note: Lubavitch.com, 8 Dec 2003: Rabbi Eliezer and Chanie Zalmanov 'have recently arrived in the region to reestablish the Chabad-Lubavitch Center of Northwest Indiana'; they 'replace Rabbi Aryeh and Tamara Dudovitz, the directors of Chabad from 1995 to 2003'.

2639965.name: Chabad at Purdue
2639965.note: Chabad on Campus (1 Dec 2014): Rabbi Levi and Adina Tiechtel moved to Indiana in November 2014 to open a Chabad House at Purdue, its first permanent presence there. Rabbi Avremel and Shaindy Gluck since July 2019 (its own site).

3779106.name: Chabad of Greater South Bend
3779106.note: No dated source found; its own site gives no year. therebbesimpact.com: the center and Schneur & Sari Gansburg, 2017; chabad.org's listing number (3779106) is from about 2017 too. Its IRS registration dates from March 2019.

5153625.name: Fort Wayne Chabad Jewish Center
5153625.note: Jewish Federation of Fort Wayne: Chabad of Fort Wayne was founded in 2021, led by Rabbi Levi and Leah Danow.

7492620.name: Chabad of Fishers-Noblesville
7492620.note: COLlive, Oct 20 2026 ('New Shluchim to Establish Chabad of Fishers, Indiana'): 'Rabbi Uri and Yehudis Libersohn, together with their son Mendel, will be moving to Fishers-Noblesville, Indiana, to establish a new Chabad Center ... under the leadership of Head Shliach Rabbi Avi Grossbaum' (also Chabadinfo.com). A report from the year itself.

117977.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Tennessee
117977.note: Lubavitch.com (11 Sept 2007, via CrownHeights.info): 'When Chabad of Memphis opened in 1994, it found a close-knit Jewish community of 10,000'. Rabbi Levi and Rivka Klein (therebbesimpact.com: 1994).

118476.name: Chabad of Knoxville
118476.note: Podcast profile: Rabbi Yossi and Miriam Esther Wilhelm 'moved to Knoxville, TN in 2001'. therebbesimpact.com: 2001.

211894.name: Chabad of Nashville
211894.note: Its own site: 'established in 1999' (Rabbi Yitzchok and Esther Tiechtel). Long before, the Frierdiker Rebbe had sent Rabbi Zalman Posner to Nashville (1949), who started the Akiva day school; not a Chabad house.

384002.name: Stanford Eisenberg Knoxville Jewish Day School
384002.note: Knox News (via CrownHeights.info, 19 Oct 2006): 'The school, which opened in August, currently serves a combined kindergarten and first-grade class'; Miriam Esther Wilhelm its head. Named for the father of a donor (seed money $150,000).

582611.name: Rohr Chabad House at Vanderbilt
582611.note: Lubavitch.com (24 Oct 2007, via CrownHeights.info): 'Chabad Opens Student Center At Vanderbilt University', Rabbi Shlomo and Nechama Rothstein its new representatives (comments: 'finally its official', 'we can't wait for you to come'). The Jewish Observer (Dec 2024): they began 17 years ago.

957897.name: Chabad-Lubavitch of Chattanooga
957897.note: Chabad.org / CrownHeights.info: Rabbi Shaul and Rosie Perlstein arrived in Chattanooga from Brooklyn in 2009 and have co-directed the Chabad Jewish Center since then; first on Pisgah Ave., later a former Masonic Lodge (2015).

6549164.name: Chabad of Williamson County
6549164.note: The Jewish Observer (Nashville), Oct 2024: 'New Chabad center opens in Williamson County' (Cool Springs), Rabbi Mendel and Chana Baron, the county's first Chabad house. chabad.org's listing number (6549164) is from late 2024 too.

117623.name: Chabad-Lubavitch of Louisiana
117623.note: Its own history page: 'In November of 1975' the Rebbe sent Rabbi Zelig and Bluma Rivkin to New Orleans (a Chabad.org obituary's 1973 is an outlier; therebbesimpact.com also has 1973). Chabad House Uptown near Tulane from 1975-76; Metairie branch 1990; Southern Mississippi Aug 2014; Baton Rouge Aug 2015.

174119.name: Tulane Chabad
174119.note: The Uptown Chabad House by Tulane: Rabbi Zelig Rivkin recalls they 'opened the Chabad House on Purim of 1976' after renovating it (the Jewish Women's Archive also has 1976). Chabad of Louisiana's own page says it began working out of it in fall 1975.

3517860.name: Undergraduate Program at Tulane University
3517860.note: Tulane News, Sept 2015: Rabbi Leibel and Mushka Lipskier 'have taken over undergraduate programming at the Rohr Chabad Jewish Student Center at Tulane University'; the Rivkins moved to graduate students.

119695.name: Slater Torah Academy

University Drive, Tamarac, bought for $4 million for fall 2007. School listings: first year fall 2005.

118265.name: Chaya Aydel Seminary

GuideStar's ruling year 2004.

117534.name: Chabad of Plantation
117534.note: Rabbi Mendy and Chanie Posner founded Chabad of Plantation in 1993 in a small storefront of about 800-900 sq ft (COLlive; Chabad.org: 'a small 900-square-foot storefront'); the new 12,000 sq ft building at 10165 Cleary Road: groundbreaking Aug 2008, moved in June 2010 (Sun-Sentinel repost).

earlier.where: a small storefront (about 800-900 sq ft), Plantation

117587.name: Aventura Chabad
117587.note: Founded by Rabbi Casriel and Ziporah Brusowankin in 1970 to serve North Dade (COLlive; Chabad.org: they came to South Florida in 1970 and served North Miami for over 40 years). Its first location was a trailer on the same grounds (Lubavitch.com, groundbreaking for a new building, Dec 2024). Rabbi Laivi and Chani Forta have co-directed for about 25 years. (The city of Aventura dates from 1995; therebbesimpact.com says 1975.)

earlier.where: a trailer on the same grounds

117589.name: Chabad of West Boca Raton
117589.note: West Boca's program guide: Rabbi Zalman and Chani Bukiet moved to Boca Raton in 1989 to establish a Chabad center (with the Denburgs, Central Boca); 'In 1989 Chabad opened centers in Central and West Boca'. Its building was finished in 2016 (Clio).

117598.name: Merkos Lubavitch of Florida
117598.note: The Florida regional office of Merkos L'Inyonei Chinuch, now Chabad's headquarters at 1140 Alton Road. Chabad.org (17 July 2025, Rabbi Avraham Korf's obituary): the Miami Herald of 2 Dec 1960 reported that Merkos 'has opened a Florida regional branch' with Korf in charge; another Chabad.org piece gives his arrival as 14 Nov 1960 (Chabadpedia says 1961). Where the office first was is not said; Friends of Lubavitch of Florida (its later umbrella) has its IRS ruling from March 1983.

117594.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Fort Lauderdale
117594.note: Rabbi Moishe Meir and Penina Lipszyc 'moved to Fort Lauderdale in 1990 to establish a Chabad center' (Chabad.org); the City of Fort Lauderdale's 'Chabad Drive' renaming (2024) dates it to 1990; one profile says the Rebbe sent them in 1989. On the Galt Mile (NE 35th Street, now Chabad Drive).

117593.name: Chabad of Pinellas County
117593.note: Its own site: Chabad of Pinellas County (Young Israel-Chabad) was established in 1988; Rabbi Shalom and Chanie Adler have directed it for more than 20 years, 'first in Clearwater, and now at 3696 Fisher Road in Palm Harbor'; their son Rabbi Pinchas Adler leads it now.

earlier.where: Clearwater

117597.name: Chabad of Greater Orlando
117597.note: Heritage Florida Jewish News (COLlive, 1 Jan 2010): 'This year, Chabad of Greater Orlando will celebrate 25 years of service in Orlando. Since its inception in 1985'; the Dubovs 'were chosen as ambassadors ... shortly after they wed in September 1984'. Heritage (2019): established in 1985. Its own site says 'founded in 1984' (the year of the appointment). Began in a small storefront.

earlier.where: a storefront on Highway 436, Casselberry
708 Lake Howell Road, Maitland

117596.name: Synagogue of Inverrary - Chabad
117596.note: Chabad.org, 23 June 2015 (Aishel House): the idea 'came to Rabbi Aron Lieberman, who has led our congregation since 1982' (caption: 'had led the congregation since 1982'). COLlive, 15 Nov 2018: the Inverrary community was 'Founded over 33 years ago and led by Shliach Rabbi Aron Lieberman', which agrees. 6700 NW 44th Street. therebbesimpact.com: 1993 (unsourced, wrong).

117602.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Sarasota & Manatee Counties
117602.note: Sarasota Herald-Tribune (via CrownHeights.info, 26 Dec 2005): 'Shortly after moving here from California in 1990, Steinmetz...'. CrownHeights.info, 28 Feb 2006 (its 11th annual dinner): Chabad's headquarters was 'the small guest room in Rabbi Steinmetz' apartment' when he 'first arrived to the city 15 years ago'.

earlier.where: a guest room in Rabbi Chaim Steinmetz's apartment

117889.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Northeast Florida
117889.note: Chabad.org, 16 Nov 2010: Rabbi Yoseph and Rivkie Kahanov 'have lived in Jacksonville for 18 years' (so 1992); Anash later: they 'built and served the greater Jacksonville community for over 30 years'. A 2011 blog calls him its founder. The Mandarin center (an acre and a half) more than doubled in 2010.

117592.name: Lubavitch Hebrew Academy
117592.note: COLlive, 4 Sept 2024: Rabbi Yossie Denburg, 'the founder and dean of LHA': 'As we begin our 40th year of service ... the Rebbe's Bracha to my wife and I in 5745, for Hatzlacha for Chinuch in Broward County' (a 40th year in 2024-25 gives a first year of 1985-86). School listings: founded in 1985. (Earlier called the Hebrew Academy Community School.)

559661.name: South Florida Jewish Academy
559661.note: Chabad.org (via CrownHeights.info, 27 Aug 2007): the new South Florida Jewish Academy for children with special needs began classes on Monday, Aug. 20 (2007), with 15 children, in the building of the former South Florida Academy of Learning, which Chabad of Coconut Creek & West Pompano Beach bought in April with the Tabacinic family's help.

117601.name: Chabad Chayil - Highland Lakes Jewish Center
117601.note: Founded 'in the late 1980s' by Rabbi Dovid Bryn (South Florida Sun Times; the Jewish Press: 'the local Chabad center in the 1980's'); after his death in 2002 Rabbi Moishe and Layah Kievman have led it (Chabad.org, Jan 2022). Exact year not found yet.

117948.name: Hollywood Community Synagogue - Chabad
117948.note: COLlive, 3 July 2015: after the eviction on Tisha B'Av 5774 (Aug 2014), Rabbi Joseph Korf said the restart 'was 1990 all over again', i.e. as when they began; the center was reclaimed on 12 Tammuz 5775 (June 2015). The Sun-Sentinel had it moving out of its house at 2215 N. 46th Ave. therebbesimpact.com: the center and Joseph & Elisheva Korf 1990. Only indirect: to check.

117960.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Southwest Broward
117960.note: COLlive, 18 July 2022: 'After a unique and life changing blessing from the Rebbe 31 years ago, Rabbi Pinny and Gitty moved to Florida to be trailblazing shluchim, opening Chabad of Southwest Broward (SWB) in Cooper City', 'operating out of a small modest modular trailer for 30 years' (so 1992). IRS: 'Chabad Lubavitch Of Southwest Broward Inc', exempt from Dec 1993 (ProPublica). therebbesimpact.com: the couple 1992, the center 1993.

earlier.where: a small modular trailer, Cooper City

117969.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Greater Daytona
117969.note: Its own site: established in 1993; COLlive: Rabbi Pinchas Ezagui 'has been in Daytona since 1993'; news of 2008-10 ('15 years', '17 years') agree.

117991.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Greater Boynton Beach
117991.note: Its own pages: Rabbi Sholom and Dinie Ciment 'arrive in Boynton in 1994'; its mission statement: founded 1994 with a handful of members. (Sun-Sentinel, May 2008: small 'thirteen years ago'.)

118196.name: Chabad Jewish Center of the Florida Keys
118196.note: Chabad.org, 22 Feb 2010 ('Florida Jews Mark Half a Century of Chabad Activities'): Rabbi Yaakov Zucker 'arrived as a newlywed in 1995, sent there by the Korfs', and directs the Chabad Jewish Center of the Florida Keys and Key West.

118198.name: Chabad of Weston Center for Jewish Life
118198.note: Our City Weston (Feb 2023): Chabad of Weston 'has been serving the local Jewish community since it first opened in 1996' (Rabbi Yisroel and Leah Spalter). Its new 16,000 sq ft center was built while it ran from a trailer for two years (Lubavitch.com).

118284.name: Chabad Jewish Center of Martin & S. Lucie County
118284.note: 10 Sept 2018: Rabbi Shlomo and Daniella Uminer's Chabad center, 'which they founded when they moved here from Brooklyn 23 years ago' (so 1995); Lubavitch.com, separately: they have led the community for 23 years. IRS: 'Chabad Jewish Center Of Martin-St Lucie County Inc', exempt from Feb 2001. (therebbesimpact.com: 1999.) A 2.5-acre campus on Sunset Trail, Palm City.

118287.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Sunny Isles Beach
118287.note: Its CYP page: 'Our synagogue began as Sunny Isles Chabad in 1994 even before Sunny Isles Beach was incorporated or named as a city', in 'a small office space on the second floor of the RK Plaza at 170th Street'; 'Various moves followed until eventually, the congregation moved to the ground floor of the King David in 2004.' Confirmed by the IRS record: 'Chabad Center Of Sunny Isles Inc', exempt from Aug 1994 (ProPublica). Rabbi Yisrael and Toby Baron.

earlier.where: an office on the second floor of RK Plaza, 170th Street
the ground floor of the King David

118356.name: Chabad Lubavitch of the Panhandle - Tallahassee
118356.note: Chabad-Lubavitch of the Panhandle 'was established in 2000' by Rabbi Schneur Zalman and Chanie Oirechman, for FSU students and Tallahassee (news of the May 2022 fire that destroyed its building; Lubavitch.com). Panama City Beach, Destin and Pensacola grew from it.

118367.name: Chabad of East Boca Raton
118367.note: Boca Raton Tribune (May 2010, its 10th anniversary): Chabad of Boca Raton appointed Rabbi Ruvi and Ahuva New to open an East Boca branch in September 1999; it began in their living room, then a storefront on Palmetto Park Road, then from 2002 a larger rented facility; a site at 770 East Palmetto Park Road was gifted by Irving and Judy Litwak.

earlier.where: Rabbi Ruvi and Ahuva New's living room
a storefront on Palmetto Park Road
a larger rented facility

118379.name: Lubavitch Chabad Jewish Student Center
118379.note: Chabad.org: Rabbi Berl and Chanie Goldman have seen Jewish life at UF grow 'since they first arrived in 2000'; a 2010 report: 'ten years after moving to Gainesville to establish a student Jewish center'. Early on it ran from tents, trailers and temporary buildings; the 23,000 sq ft Tabacinic center at 2021 NW Fifth Ave. came later.

118475.name: Chabad of Coral Springs
118475.note: Anash ('Chabad of Coral Springs celebrates 36 years and counting'): 'Established in 1986, Chabad of Coral Springs began when Rabbi Yossi Denburg and his wife Rivka were sent to South Florida' to build a Hebrew day school and a Chabad House; Rabbi Avraham Friedman became executive director in 1991. (Coral Springs Talk counted its 36th anniversary in 2023, and therebbesimpact.com says 1987: a year later.)

118411.name: Chabad Key Biscayne Jewish Center
118411.note: Lubavitch.com, 11 Nov 2002: 'three years ago, Rabbi Yoel and Rivka Caroline began introducing various Jewish activities' on Key Biscayne (so 1999); Chabad of Key Biscayne 'moved into a home of its own just in time Rosh Hashana 5763' (Sept 2002) at 211 Greenwood Drive. IRS: 'Chabad Of Key Biscayne Inc', exempt from May 2002. Now 101 Harbor Drive (Rabbi Avremel Caroline).

earlier.where: 211 Greenwood Drive, Key Biscayne

118437.name: Chabad of South Orlando
118437.note: Heritage Florida Jewish News, 3 Apr 2015: 'After having a presence in the southwest Orlando area for 15 years' (so 2000); Chabad.org, separately: 'the 2000 arrival of Rabbi Yosef and Chani Konikov'. (Chabad of Greater Orlando's history has them hired in 1998; a 2016 Heritage piece says 1999; an Anash account says activities began in 2001 from their rented home.) Earlier on Tamarind Circle; the Center of Jewish Life at 7347 Sand Lake Road from about 2015.

earlier.where: Tamarind Circle, Orlando

118514.name: Downtown Jewish Center Chabad
118514.note: Its own home page has both: 'DJCC has been serving the Fort Lauderdale community since 2000' and 'Rabbi Schneur & Devorah Kaplan, emissaries of the Lubavitcher Rebbe, founded the Downtown Jewish Center Chabad in 2003.' Directory listings (Las Olas Boulevard association; MapQuest) also say 2000. The earlier year is used; the two disagree, so medium. (VIN News, 2009: then not on chabad.org's list.) 900 E Broward Blvd.

118594.name: Chabad Russian Center of S. Florida
118594.note: Miami Herald (via CrownHeights.info, 17 Dec 2007): Rabbi Alexander Kaller 'came into town in 2002'; the synagogue 'humbly started off in 2002' in the rabbi's living room, moved after a few months to the meeting room at the Oceania condos, then to a 65-seat storefront synagogue in a strip mall; its waterfront center opened in 2026.

the meeting room at the Oceania condos
a storefront synagogue in a strip mall, Sunny Isles Beach

118653.name: Chabad at the Beaches

118646.name: Chabad of Naples

118534.name: Chabad @ University of Miami

118658.name: Chabad Jewish Center of Jupiter

119832.name: Chabad Ocean Synagogue

Sea Air Towers
Hallmark Condominiums

118660.name: California Club Chabad

(A tribute calls the late Rabbi Dovid Bryn, d. 2002, founder of 'the California Club Shul' too: an earlier minyan there, perhaps.)

earlier.where: a mall, California Club area

160742.name: Chabad of Brandon & South Shore

169223.name: Chabad at Florida International University

10031 SW 15 Terrace

earlier.where: Rabbi Mendy and Chanie Bukiet's home, East County
rented space at schools and office buildings

223658.name: Chabad of Cape Coral

earlier.where: the Labkowskis' living room

212291.name: Chabad of Bonita Springs, Estero & FGCU

an office suite in a strip mall off Old 41 Road (Bernwood Centre), Bonita Springs

118571.name: Chabad Jewish Center

a leased storefront, 6151 Central Ave.

257624.name: Chabad of Venice & North Port
257624.note: Sun Herald (CrownHeights.info, 19 Aug 2005): 'When Rabbi Sholom Schmerling and his wife, Rivka, arrived in North Port four months ago' ... 'then opened the Chabad of Venice and North Port in June'. Herald-Tribune (Sept 2005): 'Until they can raise enough money for a permanent building, the center will be based in their home.' Herald-Tribune (CrownHeights.info, March 2016): 'started ... with a handful of people in their living room in 2005'; land for the campus bought 2012.

earlier.where: the Schmerlings' home, North Port

384721.name: Chabad of Palm Beach Gardens
384721.note: Its own site: 'Chabad of Palm Beach Gardens was founded on April 30, 2006'. Timber Trace Elementary School (services), then Downtown at the Gardens and Loehmann's Plaza

325854.name: Chabad of Pembroke Pines
325854.note: Sun-Sentinel (CrownHeights.info, 6 Oct 2011): 'Andrusier, who's originally from Brooklyn, NY, founded the synagogue in 2005'; in 2011 it was still 'moving from a rented location to a more permanent place'.

371894.name: Chabad of West Pasco
371894.note: Suncoast News (CrownHeights.info, 24 Dec 2013): 'Nearly eight years ago, Rabbi Yossi and Dina Eber started out in a rented three-bedroom house in Trinity, Florida that served as both their home and synagogue. As attendance grew, they rented space in the Trinity Oaks' shopping center; a permanent home in 2013-14. Chabad.org (July 2013): they 'moved to the area more than seven years ago'; co-directors 'since 2006'. A grand opening at 9945 Trinity Blvd. was in 2009.

earlier.where: a rented three-bedroom house in Trinity (home and synagogue)
Trinity Oaks shopping center, 9945 Trinity Blvd.

347029.name: Chabad Jewish Center of Doral
347029.note: Miami Herald (CrownHeights.info, 16 Oct 2006, at Sukkot): 'Since their arrival in Doral a year ago, the Brashevitzky family has welcomed ... worshipers for weekly Chabad services held at their home, 5353 NW 109th Ct.'; 'One year ago, he established the Chabad Jewish Center in Doral' (fall 2005). IRS: 'Chabad Jewish Center Of Doral Inc', exempt from June 2006. (Later counts are a year short: Miami Herald, May 2009, 'three years later'; Doral Family Journal, 23 March 2013, 'established seven years ago'.) earlier.where: the Brashevitzkys' home, 5353 NW 109th Ct.
a shopping center, 9725 NW 41st St.

334256.name: Chabad of Southside

Rabbi Shmuel (Shmuli) and Chana Novack; early on in rented meeting rooms and libraries; the 12,000 sq ft center opened in 2019.

312032.name: Chabad of Charlotte County
312032.note: Chabad.org (CrownHeights.info, 4 Oct 2022): 'The very first was also established with a Hurricane—Hurricane Charley in 2004. 'After growing out of the in-home Chabad House, the Jacobsons began renting a storefront, where they held services and activities for nine years before purchasing the new 9,500 square foot building', moved in just before Rosh Hashanah 2022: 'the community's third Chabad House building'.

a rented storefront

298937.name: Lubavitch Aventura South

269188.name: Chabad of Deerfield Beach

Start year not found yet; lead: therebbesimpact.com 2004.

118666.name: Chabad of West Palm Beach
118666.note: Lubavitch.com 'New Appointments' (25 Aug 2004): 'West Palm Beach, Florida: Rabbi and Mrs. Mendy Kornfeld.' The chabad.org listing (118666) and therebbesimpact.com also point to 2004. 118350.name: Chabad House in Miami Beach and Chabad House on Wheels
118350.note: Miami Herald (COLlive, 24 July 2011): 'Katz's RV ministry, Chabad on Wheels, started 12 years ago, when he was completing rabbinical school in New York' (count back: 1999); 'Katz has opened a bricks-and-mortar synagogue on Lincoln Lane'. IRS: 'Chabad House On Wheels', Rabbi Zev Katz, ruling June 2002.

290969.name: Chabad of N.E. Hollywood & Dania

1335573.name: Chabad of Clay County
1335573.note: First Coast Chabad blog (8 March 2011) announced the new Clay County center, the first Jewish institution of any kind in the county, with Rabbi Shmuly and Shaina Feldman. Clay Today (CrownHeights.info, 22 June 2011): 'Since the Feldmans moved to Fleming Island in April they have hosted several events'.

1241523.name: Chabad of Clearwater
1241523.note: TampaBay.com (CrownHeights.info, 30 Oct 2011): 'A 600-square-foot space nestled in a cluster of offices off Gulf-to-Bay Boulevard is slowly materializing into ... a new Chabad center, the third in Pinellas County'; 'The Clearwater center will celebrate its grand opening at 1 p.m. Sunday.' the Tabacinic Chabad Center

1274159.name: Chabad Jewish Center of West Boynton and West Lake Worth

COLlive, 2 June 2013 (Greater Boynton's 18th gala): 'A new satellite Boynton Chabad center has opened, directed by Rabbi & Mrs. Yosef Raichik, in the western part of the city.'

1269573.name: Las Olas Chabad Jewish Center
1269573.note: Chabad.org (22 Nov 2011): 'Last December, Rabbi Chaim and Chaya Mushka Slavaticki moved to Fort Lauderdale, Fla., to open a new Chabad-Lubavitch center'; they were 'getting ready to open the doors to a rented storefront they're calling the Chabad Jewish Center of Fort Lauderdale Beach'. 2480687.name: Chabad of the Emerald Coast
2480687.note: Destin Log (CrownHeights.info, 13 Oct 2013): 'Chabad-Lubavitch recently opened a new branch on Florida's Emerald Coast.
